findings.one_line: The smoothing witness asserts membership for every fixed nonempty class merely by taking its bump small, but nonemptiness does not provide slack in the Holder radius, response range, or two-sided-modulus bounds; at a boundary class a nonzero compactly supported bump need not remain in the class. Prove a boundary-compatible construction or state the lower channels only under explicit interior slack assumptions.

Its rare-block spacing pair relies on the same unproved claim that a nonzero local bump can be added while preserving the fixed Holder ball and both fixed modulus inequalities. A nonempty class need not have that perturbation slack, so the claimed lower bound for every compatible nonempty class is not discharged.

The iid spacing construction imports the unsupported bump-preservation assertion from the general embedding; consequently its all-nonempty-class spacing lower channel is not established without an explicit interiority/slack condition or a boundary-valid alternative.
